items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: So I finished up my studying with Roy. I went to Roy. Roy was just like Preston. I mean, he was just interested in kids and youngsters and he tried to pass on all his knowledge to me.

ctx.x: Is he still around? No, he passed.

He passed about four years ago in Milwaukee. He was a terrific trumpet man. In fact, at that time, his band was considered the number two band in Chicago. Joe Oliver was first, and Bernie was number two. And Preston was playing with him, Preston Jackson. Yeah, he was right. And they were a perfect team. Well, they'd worked together for years and years. Preston and Oscar. And he always had a good band, terrific drummers. And, you know. So I would go to this Red Mill Hall, and I would just sit under Preston all…
The technique that man had was just terrific.

items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: Yeah, he took a couple of lessons. He didn't stay, but he took enough to learn to play pretty good.

ctx.x: There's one other New Orleans tromboneist here, Albert Wynn. Do you know that?
Yeah, he took a couple of lessons. He didn't stay, but he took enough to learn to play pretty good. He plays pretty good.

What's one of them? He's around. He, uh, up in our place where a friend, we have a piano, sort of a studio, not a real big recording studio, but some bands used to come up and rehearse. And about a year ago, he was there with a few people. Oh, yeah? I can't remember who, oh, Jasper Taylor. Yeah, Jasper Taylor, yeah. He was with him. He was with him.
